client-agent.note: The client assistant prepares literal copy, images and the structured catalog spec. Preparation is client-side; the platform does not research or adapt images for site production.

client-preview.note: The preview and original asset bytes are bound to the approved spec. No arbitrary styles, scripts or server-side fetching are authorized.

client-approval.note: The client obtains human approval before submission. The approval declaration asserts approval; it is not a new human-signature protocol.

client-submit.note: Submission enters the authenticated platform. Selecting this boundary opens stage 2.

client-signed.note: The signed-email CLI and local seed create MIME requests for registered identities; platform key registration alone does not enroll an AWS email grant.

client-reply.note: Durable outbox work is queued to the sender, signed with ES256 and sent via SES. Locally, the SES v2-to-v1 bridge captures unchanged MIME. No real inbox delivery.

gate-auth.note: Better Auth manages login and OAuth consent. Consent grants a scoped connector mandate; it does not approve a particular site or deployment.

gate-mcp.note: The implemented MCP connector authenticates resource-bound calls and exposes role-scoped tools. It is separate from future customer MCP products.

gate-owner.note: Verified platform roles and live imported-site email membership restrict requests and queued provider work. Site grants never confer global roles.

gate-confirm.note: Catalog approval remains unchanged. Imported deployments require exact release confirmation, passing bound reports, no drift and independently enabled deployment/handoff flags.

gate-policy.note: Versioned policies and atomic reservations enforce bounded changes. CMS content edits do not consume site-change allowance; unknown deployments retain reservations.

gate-build.note: Authorized site work enters the durable build queue. Selecting this boundary opens stage 3.

gate-email.note: Signed email validates the registered grant, signature, expiry, destination and replay before durable admission. This is independent of platform OAuth.

gate-admission.note: Email admission applies operating flags and per-partner/day limits; runtime reserves $1 per task against $10 monthly model allowance, with two global concurrent tasks.

engine-validate.note: Catalog specifications and assets follow their fixed policy. Imported-static bundles have bounded safe paths/canonical base64 and server-calculated hashes, with no uploaded build scripts.

engine-jobs.note: Postgres persists catalog and imported verification/deploy/rollback/usage jobs, admission audits and eligibility snapshots. Unknown provider outcomes block replay.

engine-astro.note: Deterministic rendering uses the fixed catalog and approved tokens. Prepared assets are copied byte-identically; source and output hashes bind the artifacts.

engine-verify.note: Secret-free hosted Agents verification uses fixed trusted checkers. Imported prebuilt files bypass Astro generation and require baseline byte/visual/interaction parity. Cloud proof remains separate.

engine-artifacts.note: The existing private bucket retains prepared bytes, verification reports and screenshots. Source and assets of imported clients remain private.

engine-host.note: Only verified bytes and a newly checked mandate reach the provider adapter. Selecting this boundary opens stage 4.

engine-receipt.note: The signed-email foundation follows SES receipt storage and SNS/SQS into intake. The local receipt-rule adapter executes the synthesized S3/SNS actions; it does not receive internet SMTP.

engine-state.note: Durable task/outbox state and DynamoDB Streams enqueue work. Tasks/outbox retain 30 days; replay/audit retain 90 days; DLQs retain 14 days. Expiration is asynchronous.

engine-analysis.note: Production workers analyze a brief, store results, delete provider sessions and release concurrency. The local OpenAI stand-in returns a fixed fictional fixture; this is not the catalog build engine.

engine-data.note: Authenticated inputs and results remain private. Accepted content retains 30 days and abandoned pending inputs seven days; lifecycle deletion is asynchronous.

hosting-customer.note: Carlos Olivera Terrazas reports the customer-site build/hosting pilot deployed and still in progress. This task has not independently inspected a hosted end-to-end transcript or customer site. Earlier local verification and independent cloud gates remain separate.

hosting-railway.note: Catalog sites use dedicated guarded projects. Imported-static sites preserve an exact owner-registered protected target; no workspace migration or CMS provision occurs.

hosting-caddy.note: Caddy serves catalog and imported static bytes. Imported serving configuration and runtime digest are pinned; original routes, headers and files must remain equivalent.

hosting-cms.note: PocketBase belongs only to catalog sites. Imported sites with cmsMode:none create no CMS service, volume, credentials, backup configuration or routes.

hosting-editor.note: Content edits use the authenticated CMS editor and do not consume site-change allowance. Client account creation and privileged CMS settings are blocked.

hosting-domain.note: The adapter observes deployment/domain/certificate state; DNS is not changed by the site tool. Live provider readiness remains an independent verification question.

hosting-s3.note: The project landing and release snapshots use private S3. The existing LocalStack quickstart serves this normal website build; it does not deploy customer Railway sites.

hosting-cdn.note: CloudFront delivers the project landing with origin access control, cache and security headers. Public TLS/DNS and cloud caching are outside LocalStack.

ops-agent.note: Repository engineering is a governed contribution workflow, not autonomous work performed by the legacy brief-analysis service.

ops-broker.note: The enabled development broker issues fixed repository-scoped App tokens. Locally it mints against fake GitHub; PR requests are recorded without real publication.

ops-pr.note: PR checks and the external App-bound policy evaluate sensitive paths and current-head approval. The advisory local integration workflow remains blocked from App publication by missing workflow-write permission.

ops-approval.note: Only Carlos Olivera Terrazas can approve the current sensitive-path head. Automation cannot manufacture approval; repository auto-merge remains disabled.

ops-main.note: An approved merge permits main CI website delivery. PR jobs cannot deploy; infrastructure activation remains separately owner controlled.

ops-release.note: Website delivery uploads the normal build, checks MIME/checksums/cache and restores a release snapshot after failed verification. Preparing this page is not live publication.

ops-watchdog.note: The one-minute watchdog reconciles runtime, cleanup and outbox work and observes committed model dollars. Real scheduled Lambda activity is tested locally.

ops-controls.note: Application allowance is $1/task and $10/month; the model warning is $8. Failures/DLQ depth alarm at one; AWS $15 notification thresholds are 50/80/100 percent. Storage/state/log retention is 7/30/90 days with 14-day DLQs. TTL/lifecycle expiry is asynchronous. Billing budgets and owner notifications are cloud-only and are not hard spending caps.

ops-admin.note: Superadmin manages testers and imported-site email grants through chat/MCP. Site administrators are scoped to assigned sites and do not change platform roles.

ops-audit.note: Durable audits and exact-ID reconciliation cover imported releases and recovery. Private reports retain effective owner-role eligibility and daily Railway costs/resource windows, including exempt sites; missing costs remain unavailable.

ops-support.note: Separate support storage/ledger/queue/worker handles human messages; SES feedback updates delivery/suppression. Support content/ledger retains seven days, logs 30 days and DLQs 14 days. The signed-agent fixture does not establish support inbox delivery.

ops-future.note: Payments/checkout and future customer apps, MCP products and plugins remain planned. This excludes the implemented platform MCP connector and the in-progress deployed website pilot.
